## What this is

Six years of independent research into the Riemann zeta function, written up honestly. Not a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis — the odds of any independent effort resolving a 150-year-old open problem are close to zero, and this site says so plainly rather than around the edges.

What it is instead: a documented account of repeatedly attacking the same obstruction from six different angles, in close collaboration with large language models, with real — if partial — technical results along the way. Some of those results stand on their own regardless of whether the central question ever closes: a geometric picture of how truncated zeta sums behave, an empirical regularity checked against 100,000 real zeros, an identity that looked like numerical coincidence until it turned out to be exact.

The throughline is process over product. There's no shortage of "I think I proved the Riemann Hypothesis" content online. There's a real shortage of careful, transparent accounts of what multi-year independent mathematical research — especially AI-assisted research — actually looks like, dead ends included.

## Who it's for

Readers comfortable with complex analysis and Dirichlet series. Specialist knowledge of zeta-function machinery isn't assumed — it gets built up the way the research itself built it up, piece by piece, over six years.

## Roadmap

The series follows the actual chronology of the research rather than a tidied-up logical order. Each entry below will link to its post as it's written.

**0 · Prologue — why this, why alone, why with an LLM** <span class="status-badge done">posted</span>

What the Riemann Hypothesis is, why this project started in 2020, and what three years of human/LLM collaboration on top of that has actually looked like in practice. [Read it](posts/prologue/index.qmd).

**1 · The Moon (late 2023, three years in)** <span class="status-badge done">posted</span>

The origin: phase functions of alternating sums, Jensen-convexity pairing, and a double-sum decomposition by the parity of a prime-factorization multiplier. [Read it](posts/the-moon/index.qmd).

**2 · Finding the Spiral (Dec 2024)** <span class="status-badge done">posted</span>

Where the project's visual language is born — truncated zeta sums spiral toward a fixed center, and `M = ⌊t/π⌋` is the natural place to stop. See the [interactive figure](posts/spiral-toward-a-center/index.qmd).

**3 · The Only Special Value (2025 H1)** <span class="status-badge done">posted</span>

A stationary-phase argument for why σ = 1/2 is the unique point where two asymptotic mechanisms collide — and the first honest naming of the gap that recurs for the rest of the series. [Read it](posts/the-only-special-value/index.qmd).

**4 · Pre-tail and Tail (Sept–Oct 2025)** <span class="status-badge done">posted</span>

The cleanest empirical result in the whole project: pre-tail and tail vectors pointing in nearly opposite directions, magnitude 1/√2, checked against 100,000 real nontrivial zeros. [Read it](posts/pre-tail-and-tail/index.qmd).

**5 · Rigidity and Its Discontents (Dec 2025)** <span class="status-badge done">posted</span>

A deliberately conditional theorem, and what it means to publish a real result that depends on an unproven lemma. [Read it](posts/rigidity-and-its-discontents/index.qmd).

**6 · Only σ = 1/2, Take Four (Feb 2026)** <span class="status-badge">planned</span>

The tightest self-derived argument in the corpus, via the approximate functional equation — and a precise account of exactly which step is assumption rather than theorem.

**7 · A Season of Reinvention (Mar–May 2026)** <span class="status-badge">planned</span>

A stochastic functional equation, a Jensen-gap tipping point, and a pivot to classifying oscillatory arithmetic sums more generally — RH as one instance of a broader phenomenon.

**8 · The Critical Line Path (Jun 2026 – present)** <span class="status-badge done">posted</span>

A numerical match too good to be coincidence — and it wasn't. See [the writeup](posts/critical-line-path-identity/index.qmd).

**9 · Where This Leaves Us** <span class="status-badge">planned</span>

An honest accounting of what's proved, what's conjectural, and an open, specific invitation to readers who know their way around Euler–Maclaurin and Riemann–Siegel theory.

## Standalone notes

A few pieces of this project stand on their own without the RH framing — a numerical regularity, a technique, a derivation. These get published independently of the chapter sequence as they're finished.
